summary: Completed the evidence-backed review of Enphase Energy after its 2026-07-29 volume anomaly strengthened. The immutable ENPH/XNAS/USD identity remains unique. The adjusted close fell 28.78% over the measured month to USD 35.07 while 9.449 million shares traded at a 2.45 volume z-score. Current SEC-filed Q2 evidence shows sequential improvement in revenue and battery shipments, resilient net liquidity, and positive cash flow, but U.S. and total revenue remained below prior-year levels, safe-harbor revenue was material, and a nonrecurring tariff refund distorted GAAP margin. Normalized owner earnings and a downside-aware common-equity value remain unsupported, so the medium-confidence assessment is ineligible with valuation_unsupported. No conviction strategy was created. Exactly one dependent idea-research refresh was queued for the accepted solar, storage, and grid-flexibility relationship.

evidence.claim: Enphase's SEC-filed Q2 2026 Form 10-Q reports USD 291.854 million quarterly revenue, down 20% year over year; 113.8 MWh of battery shipments; USD 937.708 million of cash and marketable securities; USD 572.836 million of debt; USD 143.194 million of six-month operating cash flow; USD 285.022 million of inventory; USD 236.1 million of purchase obligations; and 132.145 million shares outstanding. U.S. quarterly revenue fell 16% year over year, safe-harbor shipments were USD 84.3 million, and tariff refunds added 15.6 percentage points to GAAP gross margin.

The SEC-hosted issuer release reports Q2 revenue of USD 291.9 million, USD 84.3 million of safe-harbor revenue, 113.8 MWh of battery shipments, USD 40.3 million of operating cash flow, USD 25.9 million of free cash flow, and USD 937.7 million of cash and marketable securities. U.S. revenue declined about 3% sequentially while Europe rose about 35%. Q3 guidance is USD 290-320 million of revenue, including about USD 75 million of safe-harbor shipments, and 130-150 MWh of battery shipments.
